Marathon Petroleum edged down 0.39% today despite oil prices climbing above $100 a barrel—the highest level since May—driven by escalating Iran war tensions and fears of Middle East supply disruptions. Refineries are running at 98% capacity with robust demand signals, yet the stock gave back a fraction of its strong two-week gain (up 9.83% since early September), suggesting investors may be taking profits after the recent rally or rotating away from refiner equities despite the oil price tailwind.

The disconnect hints at a broader market dynamic: while higher crude prices typically boost refiners' margins, the current spike is tied explicitly to geopolitical risk and potential supply destruction rather than fundamental demand strength. Investors appear cautious about betting further on energy assets in an environment where political rhetoric—including statements that prices won't fall until after midterm elections—is driving volatility and may be creating uncertainty about the durability of current energy market conditions.
